findings.text: blocking: the manifest declares this file as negative_control_log, but it is the green head-arm suite (4 passed, no EXIT= line and no failing test id), so the negative-control evidence cannot be admitted under the rule requiring a non-zero EXIT and at least one failing test id the head arm does not fail; no red control log exists anywhere in the run.

follow-on: the head-arm gate log carries no first line naming the revision, tree and command, and no EXIT line, so the recorded 4-passed result cannot be tied to c1e87c413; the baseline arm log likewise lacks a header, and the manifest records the arms as a prose `tests:` string rather than the baseline_suite/after_suite JSON.

follow-on: `_closed_ring` is a verbatim copy of the codec owner's scripts/prototypes/efit_field_swap/trace_record.py:128 `_closed_ring` (whose TraceRecord.wall_rings already closes rings), so the module forks a capability it could import from the owner.

follow-on: runtime code imports the private helper `_analytic_inputs` from the test module tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py, coupling the producer to a test file the brief fenced off; the analytic-input source belongs to a support owner, not a test.

follow-on: `requested = -500 if cells == 550 else -cells` remaps the requested 550-cell case to a magic -500 with no explanation, leaving the fixture-store identity the record is keyed to opaque to a reader.

follow-on: the negative-control assertion accepts `not valid` OR a class change, so it cannot show the refusal is due to the declared COCOS-17 polarity as docs/research/certified-carrier-export.html:150 claims; an unrelated geometric refusal satisfies it and it would not redden if only the polarity guard were removed.
